Section 2: Late Submission Policy and Slip Days
All programming assignments and project milestones are due at 11:59 PM IST on the
announced deadline date. Each student is granted a total of 3 grace slip days for the
entire semester, with at most 2 slip days usable on any single assignment. Once slip
days are exhausted, late submissions incur a flat penalty of 10% per day for up to 3
calendar days. Submissions more than 72 hours (3 days) past the deadline will not be
accepted and receive zero marks.

Section 3: Weekly Syllabus & Lab Requirements
Weeks 1-4 cover Uninformed & Heuristic Search (A*, Minimax) and Probabilistic Graphical
Models. Weeks 5-8 cover Supervised Learning, Neural Networks, and Transformer
Architectures. Weeks 9-12 cover Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Vector Databases
(FAISS/Chroma), Dense Embeddings (MiniLM/BGE), and Grounded Evaluation Metrics.

Section 4: CS-301 Examination Schedule and Lab Hardware
The CS-301 Mid-Semester Exam is scheduled on October 14, 2026 from 09:30 AM to 11:30 AM
in Lecture Hall Complex LHC-101. The End-Semester Exam is scheduled on December 08,
2026 from 02:00 PM to 05:00 PM in LHC-101. Mid-Semester exams are closed-book, except
students may bring one handwritten A4 double-sided formula sheet. Final Capstone
Project demos and code viva will take place on November 28, 2026 in the AI Systems Lab
(Turing Block 204).

Article 4.1: Mandatory Class Attendance Requirement
Every enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate student must maintain a minimum
attendance of 75% separately in every registered theory and laboratory course. Students
whose attendance falls below 75% will be debarred (detained) from appearing in the
End-Semester Examination for that course and awarded an 'FA' (Failure due to
Attendance) grade.

Article 8.3: Academic Integrity, Plagiarism, and Generative AI Policy
All submitted theses, lab reports, and code repositories are screened via Turnitin and
MOSS similarity checkers. Text similarity exceeding 15% (excluding bibliography and
quoted citations) constitutes academic misconduct. Use of Generative AI tools (such as
Gemini or ChatGPT) is permitted only when explicitly authorized by the course
instructor and must be accompanied by an AI Disclosure Statement detailing prompts and
verification steps.

Article 9.2: Answer Script Inspection and Revaluation
Students may apply for answer script revaluation within 7 calendar days of grade
publication by paying a revaluation fee of Rs. 500 per course. If the revised score
increases by 5% or more, the fee is fully refunded.

All residential hostel main gates close at 11:00 PM on weekdays (Sunday to Thursday)
and 11:59 PM on weekends (Friday and Saturday). Biometric attendance is recorded at the

Central Reading Room or AI Compute Lab after 11:00 PM must generate a Digital Night
Pass on the Campus Portal approved by their Faculty Advisor.

Section 3: Campus Wi-Fi (EduRoam), GPU Cluster, and Mess Rebate Policy
Every student receives a high-speed EduRoam Wi-Fi quota of 50 GB per week on the 5 GHz
campus network. Peer-to-peer torrenting and unauthorized cryptocurrency mining on
campus networks or the DGX GPU cluster lead to immediate MAC address suspension.
Students taking approved leave from campus for 5 or more consecutive days can apply for
a hostel mess rebate of Rs. 160 per day via the Student ERP at least 48 hours prior to
departure.

Financial Aid, Scholarships & Industrial Internship Guidelines (2026) 

Section 1: Merit-cum-Means (MCM) and Dean's Merit Scholarship 

The Merit-cum-Means (MCM) Scholarship provides a 50% tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend of Rs. 3,000 for ten months each academic year. To qualify for the MCM Scholarship, a student must have an annual gross family income below Rs. 6,00,000 (Six Lakhs), maintain a minimum CGPA of 7.50, and have no active disciplinary or academic backlog records. Applications close on September 30 every year.

Section 2: Semester-Long Industrial Internship & NOC Rules 

Final-year (7th or 8th semester) B.Tech students with a CGPA of 7.00 or above and zero pending backlogs are eligible to pursue a 6-month (24-week) external industrial or research internship equivalent to 12 academic credits. Students must submit an official offer letter to the Career Development Cell (CDC) at least 15 days before the internship start date to obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC).
